scope: Source-confirmed missing explicit-handler verification and two old embedded-result UI acceptance gaps

original_issue.production: ChatPresentationBridge.resolveExpansions accepted nonempty expandedHandler when canResolveHandler was nil. The modern-native fallback caller has no resolver, so it could emit a dead expansion control.
original_issue.test: The old negative UI case only launched an empty seeded chat and queried a fabricated expansion_action_unresolvable ID. The actual UI uses expansion_action_sheet/fullScreen/window. The positive case hardcoded a TextField while the original editor can be TextView, and made expansion checks optional.

changes: Explicit expandedHandler now requires positive resolver evidence. Ordinary same-content sheet/full-screen modes remain unchanged.
Existing resolver regression checks missing resolver, explicit rejection, blank handler and positive resolution alongside existing valid modes.

Original provider has an opt-in strict flow that waits for real load_skill output, newly exposed tool schema, tool_search result and actual web result before final success text; other fixtures are unchanged.
Negative fixture seeds an original persisted ChatMessages/AgentRun with native fallback content and an unavailable original owner. No network/model dispatch or fake authorization.

Both original UI methods now open the actual chat/editor, assert visible content first, assert every original call completed, require real expansion/dismissal, and reject actual dead expansion control identifiers.

test_scope.evidence_limit: HTTP model and embedded view provider are declared fixtures. This does not prove live cloud provider or a companion process.

superseded_reason: Queued native job carried missing runtime artifact input; replaced before native execution
